title: 267. why you procrastinate (even when you really care)
description_html:
do you struggle with procrastinating… even on things you truly care about?! are you aware of your worst procrastination habits but don’t know how to change them?

in this episode, i am once again joined by dr. sarah olivo and dr. liz seidler— two clinical psychologists and hosts of the college is fine, everything is fine podcast who've helped students navigate the highs and lows of college for over a decade.

this episode breaks down WHY we tend to procrastinate and HOW we can get things done more efficiently (and without all the self-judgement). whether you’re a college student who’s avoiding those upcoming assignments, a post-grad who can’t seem to balance work with life, or a life-long procrastinator hoping to change your ways, this episode is full of science-backed tips for getting things done.

how you can struggle with procrastination and still be high-functioning

whether you can be a perfectionist and still procrastinate

tips on how to stop procrastinating + get things done!
reminders for people who are hard on themselves about their procrastination

summary: sadie talks with dr. sarah olivo and dr. liz seidler, clinical psychologists and hosts of the college is fine, everything is fine podcast, about why we procrastinate even on things we care about. they frame procrastination as an emotion regulation problem more than a motivation or laziness problem, and they explain the "excuse generating machine" the brain uses to dodge dread, overwhelm, or fear of failure. they get into how adhd and executive function differences change what helps, how perfectionism shows up as over-rehearsing and rechecking, and why college is a breeding ground for procrastination compared to the built-in structure of high school. listeners come away with practical tools: the premack principle (a low-reward task first, then a reward), the carrot vs. stick idea, body doubling, picking the smallest possible next step, mood induction to shift your emotional state before starting, and reframing "lazy" as a state instead of a trait. the episode closes with reminders to stay flexible, be kind to yourself when a system stops working, and notice the strengths you already have.
quote: PROCRASTINATION really is an EMOTION REGULATION problem.
